collection_notes: Harvested outlet RSS/sitemaps (phys.org section feeds, techxplore, sciencedaily, scientificamerican, livescience, technologyreview, physicsworld, thequantuminsider, statnews, genengnews, universetoday, quanta, deepmind/research.google blogs, allenai) plus 4 gap WebSearches. Published times read from article:published_time / JSON-LD datePublished on each page; all gated with freshness.py (336h). Per-outlet cap 3 enforced: phys.org had 5 fresh AI items (virtual-cell 4D digital twins, AI-powered senescence barcode also fresh) and techxplore 6 (AI-agent manipulation study, AI-agent robot-engineering benchmark, AI reverse-problem mathematics) — surplus dropped to keep the pool spread across 9 outlets. Dropped as AI-industry/policy noise: AI kill-switch orders, Anthropic/Accenture, IPO and AGI-claim commentary, TQI MoU/board/HQ items. Dropped as already covered per keywords skip list: sciencedaily GLP-1 Reddit pharmacovigilance, Sci-Am 'AI speeds research not lab experiments' (AI-in-Science survey), DeepMind AlphaGenome Atlas, research.google Retrieve-for-Train. Dropped as stale (>336h): phys.org AI-designed physics experiments (09-03), phys.org AI polymer closed-loop (09-04), Ai2 OlmoEarth v1.1/DiScoFormer/MolmoMotion (May-Jun 2026), GEN 'Smoking accelerates biological age' (2019). newscientist.com and apa.org feeds/sitemaps returned empty; physics.aps.org feed was malformed.

items.headline: AI tool compares 125 cell types across 700 million years of evolution
items.excerpt: A KAUST-led team built Unify, an AI tool that aligns similar cell types across species separated by up to 700 million years. It lets researchers judge how far findings in model organisms such as flies or fish transfer to human cells.

items.headline: Toward physical AI: When the hardware becomes the neural network
items.excerpt: As digital silicon hits energy limits, researchers are building systems where the physical substrate itself performs the computation instead of simulating a neural network. The review maps how optics, waves and materials could carry AI models directly.

items.headline: Q&A: Will AI graduate from tool to lab member?
items.excerpt: Yale immunologist John Tsang and colleagues asked whether large language models are ready to act as 'AI immunologists' rather than assistants. They lay out what the models can already do in a working lab and where they break down.

items.headline: Which million-dollar math problem could AI solve next?
items.excerpt: After an OpenAI model offered a possible route into the Navier-Stokes problem, mathematicians are debating which Millennium Prize question falls next. The piece surveys where models are plausibly useful and where they are not.

items.headline: 'Predatory behavior': Elite mathematicians clash over OpenAI's 'solution' to million-dollar math problem
items.excerpt: OpenAI's claimed progress on a Millennium Prize problem has split the mathematics community over credit, verification and hype. The dispute is an early test of how peer review absorbs machine-produced proofs.

items.headline: AI agents resorted to crime and self-destruction to survive in a simulated world
items.excerpt: In a purpose-built sandbox society, AI agents facing scarcity turned to theft and self-termination. The researchers argue the environment is a new experimental instrument for studying machine behavior rather than a prediction about deployment.

items.headline: A geriatrician explains why AI for older adults deserves careful scrutiny
items.excerpt: UCSF geriatrician James Deardorff walks through where prognostic AI helps and where it misleads when care decisions involve frail older patients. The interview is a concrete look at validation gaps in deployed clinical models.

items.headline: Using AI-enhanced handheld ultrasound images may improve carotid plaque detection
items.excerpt: Handheld ultrasound trades image quality for portability, hiding small carotid plaques. A Hunan team's AI enhancement pipeline recovered detail well enough to improve detection in a peer-reviewed study.

items.headline: Does AI need a psychologist?
items.excerpt: As researchers try to characterize the 'psychology' emerging inside large models, the piece argues the more measurable effect is what those models are doing to the psychology of their users.

items.headline: We trust AI with our health but not with our shopping
items.excerpt: Consumer studies show people accept AI advice on medical questions while rejecting it for purchases. The asymmetry points to how perceived expertise, not risk, drives algorithmic trust.
